name: Parallel map and fold with std::thread (Modern C++ Cookbook)
listed_description: Hand-written parallel map and fold function templates that split a random-access range across hardware_concurrency() std::thread workers with no shared data, falling back to sequential below 10,000 elements.
claim_text: Parallel version is faster only above roughly 2 million elements; at 50 million elements map took 27457 us against 60049 us sequential and fold 19075 us against 41374 us.
book_benchmark: perf_timer wall-clock microseconds for sizes 10,000 to 50,000,000 ints; map doubles each element, fold sums into long long; baseline std::transform and std::accumulate. Windows 64-bit, Intel Core i7 with 4 physical and 8 logical cores; compiler and flags not stated in this recipe. Single run per size, book notes run-to-run variation.
found_in: book: Modern C++ Programming Cookbook, 3rd ed. (2024), ch. 8 Threading and Concurrency, recipe 'Implementing parallel map and fold with threads', How it works

name: Parallel map and fold with std::async tasks (Modern C++ Cookbook)
listed_description: Parallel map and fold built on std::async and std::future, one asynchronous task per hardware thread; book finds it faster than the raw std::thread version and than sequential for large ranges.
claim_text: At 50 million elements map took 22216 us against 59665 us sequential and fold 12942 us against 58689 us; faster than the thread version, especially fold.
book_benchmark: Same perf_timer harness as the thread recipe: sizes 10,000 to 50,000,000 ints, map doubles elements, fold sums; baseline sequential std::transform and std::accumulate plus the std::thread implementation. Windows 64-bit, Intel Core i7 (assumed same machine as previous recipe); compiler and flags not stated. A recursive divide-and-conquer std::async variant was also timed and was no better than sequential, so it is not a candidate.
guessed_baseline: std::transform and std::accumulate (sequential); std::thread-based parallel map and fold
found_in: book: Modern C++ Programming Cookbook, 3rd ed. (2024), ch. 8 Threading and Concurrency, recipe 'Implementing parallel map and fold with tasks', How it works and There's more

name: C++17 parallel algorithms std::transform, std::reduce, std::transform_reduce with std::execution::par
listed_description: Standard C++17 execution-policy overloads (std::execution::par) used to write map and fold in a few lines; std::transform_reduce fuses both steps and is reported as usually faster than separate map plus reduce.
claim_text: Parallel versions beat sequential for these datasets, though which is better varies with dataset size; transform_reduce, especially parallel, executes better in most cases.
book_benchmark: Timing table shown only as a figure image (numbers not in text): sequential vs parallel map and reduce, and std::transform_reduce. 64-bit release build with Visual C++ 2019 16.4.x on an Intel Xeon with four cores; flags not stated. Book warns MSVC does not parallelize copy, fill, reverse, rotate and similar algorithms, and that std::accumulate has no policy overload.
guessed_baseline: std::transform and std::accumulate (sequential); hand-rolled thread and std::async parallel map and fold
found_in: book: Modern C++ Programming Cookbook, 3rd ed. (2024), ch. 8 Threading and Concurrency, recipe 'Implementing parallel map and fold with standard parallel algorithms', How it works and There's more
